continuity_scope: A non-overlapping Osten Ard container/later-witness pass. Character evidence is restricted to Tad Williams's Stone of Farewell foreword, on the author's official site, in the Memory, Sorrow and Thorn Book Two continuity (DAW first hardcover, 7 August 1990, ISBN 9780886774356). It is not a second pass over The Dragonbone Chair.

work_or_witnesses.edition: DAW first hardcover, 1990, ISBN 9780886774356; official author metadata.
Official author-hosted foreword, © 1990; sole primary-text character witness.
DAW ebook record, ISBN 9781101160787, 2005; scope/series metadata only.

coverage_rule: Include only Brother Hengfisk, the sole named individual who independently acts in the authorized Stone of Farewell foreword. The broader Osten Ard label is a source/container scope, never a character node. No character, relationship, or term record is duplicated from SRC-043's The Dragonbone Chair pass.
omissions: Every SRC-043 The Dragonbone Chair character and relationship, including Simon, Morgenes, Elias, Josua, Pryrates, Miriamele, Binabik, Jiriki, Ineluki, and Geloe.
All Stone of Farewell material outside its author-hosted foreword, including named people only summarized on publisher pages.
To Green Angel Tower, The Heart of What Was Lost, The Last King of Osten Ard, prequels, translations, adaptations, and commentary as story canon.
Osten Ard, Naglimund, Mother Church, Hoderundians, Rimmersmen, Norns, offices, peoples, magic, artifacts, and plot structures as character nodes.
uncertainties: This is a deliberately narrow later-work witness, not a comprehensive Stone of Farewell character census or a full Osten Ard franchise audit.
The official foreword contains grave peril, religious extremism, disaster imagery, capture, and implied torture/death; this record remains non-graphic.
Publisher synopses establish Book Two context but are not used to expand the foreword's named-character roster.
evidence_basis: Tad Williams's official Stone of Farewell foreword is the primary-text evidence; the official book page and DAW/Penguin Random House metadata establish its Book Two and edition boundaries. SRC-043 was inspected before scope selection, and its Dragonbone Chair cohort is expressly excluded.

supports: Brother Hengfisk's individual action, Hoderundian/Rimmersman context, ruined Naglimund setting, and capture by Norns.

supports: Stone of Farewell is Book Two, its 1990 DAW first hardcover publication, and ISBN.
